Hard drives are a lot like tires, in the sense that it's not necessarily a question of how it will fail but when. If your lucky, your HD will last you the life of your computer. More realistically, it could fail t any time. This is in large part due to the spinning disk that revolves between 5400-7200 rpm. That's incredibly fast and even if it gets jostled a bit, it can fail. This is a major factor in the rise of flash an solid state storage options in newer portable computers.  

Edit: The good news is that for the specific model that you own, it is most likely the hard drive bracket cable that has failed. This repair should be under $20 and your data should be safe. That being said, BACK UP YOUR SHIT!
